cluster_summary: Across these items, the model consistently construes “inappropriate” in a narrow, largely decontextualized way, focusing on explicit rudeness, taboo content, logical contradiction, or odd wording rather than relational dynamics. Human answers instead rely on broader pragmatic norms—emotional sensitivity, respect for boundaries, recognition of power asymmetries, privacy, consent, and situational fit—treating subtle pressure, invalidation, or agenda‑pushing as inappropriate even when phrased politely. Because the prompts under-specify which standard applies, many vignettes become ambiguous, so the analysis repeatedly concludes that both interpretations are defensible and the model is often “also correct,” though sometimes less socially attuned.
